heldReason.note: The dictionary opens the 扁 body with a long horizontal bar — 戸, width 39 in both glyphs — where the licensed corpora draw a short dot: 戶, width 12 in 褊 and 24 in 諞. That is a different stroke, not a different direction or order, so both glyphs fail closed and stay out of the runtime and out of later queues. Same component and same treatment as 扆 and 牖 in batch 9.

corpusOverrides.note: First special grade batch with no corpus override. Every flagged glyph was measured against each corpus carrying the same stroke count and no alternative changed the flagged-stroke count, so the queue's starting corpus was kept everywhere. 褊 and 嘏 each had an alternative that shaved a few degrees off the maximum; under the rule that only a change in the flagged-stroke count is acted on, both were left alone.

directionProbe.threshold: angle over 60° between dictionary and candidate start-to-end vectors
directionProbe.note: 苹, 觱, 嘏, 醢 and 莧 were resolved by reordering and 苹, 瀌, 翯 and 徯 by an authored path. 褊 6 and 諞 8 turned out to be the 戶 form difference and were held. The endpoint assignment check found no order difference the angle probe had missed. Recomputed against the published order and paths, no stroke is over 60°.

subThresholdSlants.method: direction-probe rows recomputed against the published order and paths: 6 rows between 45° and 60°, none corrected
subThresholdSlants.note: Short opening dots and marks the dictionary draws vertically or steeper than the licensed corpora (旆 1 at 58°, 麃 1 at 58°, 襃 1 at 59°, 鑣 9 at 54°, 頏 1 at 58°, 覈 12 at 46°). Kept as licensed geometry, as in the earlier batches.

sourceTransform.note: One dictionary group carries a horizontal offset, translate(12, -830). serve.py, source-checks.mjs and direction-probe.mjs accept translate(x, -y), and the published paths come from the licensed corpus, so the offset only affects what the review sheet draws.
